getting-started.title: Find duplicate code in VS Code

transcript.title: Open Deslop in VS Code
transcript.text: I open the Extensions view and find Deslop. This is the extension that adds the duplicate-code panel to VS Code. With it installed, I open this small project so we can review one finding from beginning to end.

transcript.title: Open a finding
transcript.text: The Deslop panel lists the repeated code it found in this project. I click one finding to open its details. The file links tell me where the copies live, so I can go straight to the code instead of searching through folders.

transcript.title: Visit both copies
transcript.text: I open the first file, then the second one. Deslop takes me to the relevant lines in each file. I read the code around the highlighted section too, because two similar pieces of code may still be used in different ways.

transcript.title: Compare before editing
transcript.text: I use Compare to put the two copies side by side. Now I can see what stayed the same and what changed. This gives me a useful starting point for a cleanup, while I still decide which behavior the project needs.

description.en: Install Deslop, scan a project for duplicate code, and compare two copies in the VS Code diff editor.
description.zh: 安装 Deslop，扫描项目中的重复代码，并在 VS Code 中并排比较两处副本。

transcript.title: Create the project settings
transcript.text: I create the Deslop settings file at the root of this project. Keeping it with the code gives the team the same starting point. I save the file here, then use the sidebar to check the effect of my changes.

transcript.title: Choose what to skip
transcript.text: I add the archive folder to the exclusions and save the file. Those files are skipped when Deslop checks the project. Hiding a reported file is a different choice: it changes what I see in the results while the file is still checked.

transcript.title: Override one run
transcript.text: For a single run, I can choose a different limit on the command line. Here I ask Deslop to report without failing because of repeated code. This changes the check for this run, without rewriting the settings the team has saved.

transcript.title: Set a limit and inspect the result
transcript.text: Now I set a five-percent limit as an example and run the check again. This project is over that limit, so the command fails and still writes its report. I inspect the result to see which repeated code caused the failure.

description.en: Exclude vendor files, hide generated-only findings, and set a duplicate code threshold in .deslop.toml.
description.zh: 用 .deslop.toml 排除第三方文件、隐藏仅涉及生成代码的结果，并设置重复率阈值。

ai-integration.title: Connect a coding agent to the Deslop MCP server

transcript.title: Ask the agent before writing
transcript.text: Before asking my coding agent to write another helper, I ask it to check the project first. Here I am using pi with the Deslop connection enabled. I give it the existing file so the request is about the code I actually have.

transcript.title: Let the agent check Deslop
transcript.text: The agent reads the file and calls Deslop to look for similar code. This is a real tool call against the open project. I can see the request and the returned result in the conversation, instead of relying on the agent to guess.

transcript.title: Review the returned files
transcript.text: Deslop returns two matching files, and pi points me to them. That gives me an existing implementation to review before I create another copy. I read the file names and the reported locations, then check the source rather than stopping at the agent's summary.

transcript.title: Check the source yourself
transcript.text: I open the matching files side by side in Deslop. Now I can check the code and its differences myself. The agent helped me find a possible reuse; I still decide whether that implementation fits the change I want to make.

description.en: Configure the Deslop MCP server for a coding agent and query the workspace for duplicate code before editing.
description.zh: 为编程智能体配置 Deslop MCP 服务器，在编辑前查询工作区中的重复代码。

how-it-works.title: How Deslop finds copied and similar code

transcript.title: Find a copy worth reviewing
transcript.text: Deslop looks through the project and brings possible copies into the sidebar. I open one of those findings here. Instead of taking a number on trust, I can follow its file links and inspect the exact code that was reported.

transcript.title: See past different names
transcript.text: These two files use different names, but the calculation is the same. I open the comparison to see that directly. Renaming a class or a variable has not made the repeated work disappear, and the side-by-side view makes that easy to check.

transcript.title: Read the surrounding code
transcript.text: I visit each original file and look beyond the highlighted lines. The surrounding code tells me how the calculation is used. This is where I decide whether one shared helper would make sense, or whether the two copies should stay separate.

transcript.title: Watch the result update
transcript.text: I make an edit in the source file and save it. Deslop checks the changed project and refreshes the finding in the editor. I can compare again straight away, which keeps the review connected to the code I am actually working on.

description.en: See why renamed variables can still produce a match and how Deslop ranks duplicate code by the amount copied.
description.zh: 了解变量改名后为何仍能找到副本，以及 Deslop 如何按重复规模排序。

transcript.title: Open an Osprey finding
transcript.text: Here is an Osprey project. I open one of its files, then click a finding in the Deslop sidebar. The file links lead to the repeated code. I can review those copies in the same way as other languages.

transcript.title: Compare the Osprey files
transcript.text: I compare the two Osprey files side by side. I can see the repeated calculation and check any differences before I edit it. The useful result is the source comparison in front of me, with both copies available to inspect.

transcript.title: Select the Python-looking syntax
transcript.text: This Osprey file uses Python-looking syntax. Its leading comment tells Deslop how to read it. I open the file and its finding to check that it is treated as Osprey, while ordinary Python files keep their usual identity.

transcript.title: Save the project selection
transcript.text: I open the Osprey project file and list the Python-looking source files that belong to it. After saving the setting, I run Deslop on the project and inspect the result. That makes the choice visible in the project instead of leaving it to guesswork.

description.en: Scan Osprey code and see how a Python flavor marker or osprey.toml selects files for analysis.
description.zh: 扫描 Osprey 代码，并了解如何通过 Python 语法标记或 osprey.toml 选择要分析的文件。

github-action.title: Check duplicate code in GitHub Actions

transcript.title: Create the workflow
transcript.text: I start by creating a workflow file for this project. The first step checks out the code. I add Deslop immediately after it, so GitHub can check the files and produce a report whenever I run this workflow.

transcript.title: Choose the version
transcript.text: Here I choose the released version of Deslop that this workflow will use. I keep the version written in the file, so another release cannot silently change the check. The settings are saved alongside the rest of the project.

transcript.title: Report first, then set a limit
transcript.text: For the first run, I ask for a report without blocking the build. Once I have reviewed the result, I can set a limit. Here I use five percent as an example, then run the same check locally and inspect why it fails.

transcript.title: Check the changed code
transcript.text: For a check on new code, I save my changes to a file and select only the added lines. Deslop still looks through the project for matching copies. I read the result to see which new code caused the check to fail.

description.en: Add Deslop to GitHub Actions and fail a pull request check when the duplicate code percentage exceeds a threshold.
description.zh: 在 GitHub Actions 中运行 Deslop，当代码重复率超过阈值时让拉取请求检查失败。

vscode-cluster-panel.title: Compare duplicate code side by side in VS Code

transcript.title: Find the repeated code
transcript.text: I open a finding from the Deslop sidebar. Its details show the files containing the repeated code. I can follow either file link to see the original source, without leaving the editor or copying line numbers into a search.

transcript.title: Compare with the first copy
transcript.text: I click the comparison button beside the second copy. Deslop opens both files together, with their differences highlighted. I can read the same section on each side and check whether the differences matter before I change either file.

transcript.title: Choose two files to compare
transcript.text: When I want a different pair, I select one copy first, then choose Compare with Selected on the other. The editor opens those two files together. I can repeat this for another pair when a finding contains several copies.

transcript.title: Check the file totals
transcript.text: Back in the sidebar, I expand Duplication to see the project and file totals. The file rows help me choose where to investigate next. I open a file from that list, then return to its finding to review the actual repeated code.

description.en: Jump to each copy from a Deslop finding and compare any two occurrences in the VS Code diff editor.
description.zh: 从 Deslop 的结果跳转到每处副本，并在 VS Code 的差异编辑器中比较任意两处。

accuracy-transparency.title: How to read code duplication percentages

transcript.title: Read the project total
transcript.text: I expand the Duplication section to read the project total. Deslop shows how many lines it analysed and how many it found in repeated code. The percentage describes those files; it does not tell me that a cleanup is automatically safe.

transcript.title: Follow the file counts
transcript.text: I open the file rows behind that total and inspect the highlighted code. This lets me connect the number to real source lines. When I review a result, I want to understand which files were checked and what work was counted.

transcript.title: Check the actual copies
transcript.text: Next I put the reported copies side by side. I check that they really repeat the same work and look at their differences. This is the evidence I use to decide what deserves attention, rather than treating a percentage as a verdict.

transcript.title: See what an exclusion changes
transcript.text: I exclude a folder in the settings file and save it. The sidebar updates because those files are no longer part of the analysis. Before comparing two results, I check settings like this so I know that both runs measured the same files.

description.en: Learn which lines count toward a duplicate code percentage and how Deslop checks its findings against known examples.
description.zh: 了解哪些代码行计入重复率，以及 Deslop 如何用已知示例检验检测结果。

research-background.title: Types of duplicate code and how to detect them

transcript.title: Start with two copies
transcript.text: Here are two files that repeat the same calculation. I open both to see where that repeated work lives. The practical question is simple: when this behavior needs a fix, will someone remember to update every copy of it?

transcript.title: Change one copy
transcript.text: I change one of the copies and save it. The other file has not changed with it. That is the maintenance problem repeated code can create: a fix in one place does not automatically reach the other places that need it.

transcript.title: See what now differs
transcript.text: I compare the files again to see the difference I just introduced. This view gives me something concrete to review with the team. I can point to the changed line, check its purpose, and decide whether the other copy needs the same change.

transcript.title: Decide what to share
transcript.text: A finding does not mean I should delete a copy automatically. I inspect both versions and the places that use them. If a shared implementation makes the code easier to maintain, I can make that change and test the behavior I intend to keep.

description.en: Compare exact copies, renamed copies, and edited copies, and see what makes a similar code finding worth reviewing.
description.zh: 对比完全相同、改名和改动过的代码副本，了解哪些相似代码值得审查。

for-ai.title: Find similar code before writing with an AI coding agent

transcript.title: Ask what is repeated
transcript.text: I ask pi to check the repeated code in this project before making a change. It calls Deslop and brings the result into the conversation. I start with one finding so the review stays small enough to understand and act on.

transcript.title: Read the files behind the result
transcript.text: I ask the agent for the files behind that finding. The reply shows where the repeated code lives and how many copies were found. I use those locations to guide the next step, rather than asking for a broad rewrite of the project.

transcript.title: Check before adding a helper
transcript.text: Before adding another helper, I ask pi to read the existing file and search for similar code. Deslop returns the matching files. This is the useful moment to spot something I can reuse, while there is still time to avoid writing another copy.

transcript.title: Review before accepting a change
transcript.text: I finish by opening the source comparison in the editor. I check that the proposed reuse preserves the behavior I need. After a focused change, I run the project's tests and review Deslop again instead of assuming the agent's first answer is enough.

description.en: Use the Deslop MCP find-similar tool to find reusable code in the live workspace, then test and check again after editing.
description.zh: 通过 Deslop MCP 的 find-similar 工具查找工作区中可复用的代码，并在修改后测试和复查。

python-click.title: Remove duplicate Python code from Click in VS Code

transcript.title: Click, open in VS Code
transcript.text: This is Click, the Python library behind thousands of command-line tools, open in VS Code with Deslop installed. Deslop has already read every Python file in the library and ranked the duplicate code it found. The worst copies sit at the top of this list, and the warning under this method says it exists more than once.

transcript.title: Compare two exceptions
transcript.text: Near the top, Deslop pairs two exception classes: No Such Option and No Such Command. Compare puts them side by side. The constructor, the default message and the close-match suggestions are the same code. The only change is that option became command, all the way through.

transcript.title: Three identical methods
transcript.text: This finding is exact. The Bash, Z shell and PowerShell completion classes each define the same get completion args method, line for line. I follow each file link to read the copies in place before I change anything.

transcript.title: Remove the copies
transcript.text: The other two classes can reuse the Bash method directly, so I replace both copies with one line each and save. Deslop scans again straight away and the finding is gone. Then I run the shell completion tests from Click, and all fifty eight still pass.

description.en: Deslop finds real duplicate code in Click's Python source, compares the copies side by side, and removes one with a two-line refactor while Click's tests still pass.
description.zh: Deslop 在 Click 的 Python 源码中找到真实的重复代码，并排比较副本，再用两行重构删除其中一处，Click 的测试依然通过。
